1) the informedia video search system is an effective tool for searching video, 2) the informedia interface allows the user to quickly find relevant video, 3) the informedia system is scalable, and 4) the informedia search system can be applied to many types of video.

1) a video retrieval system that is based on automatic analysis of video content can be made very efficient by allowing a human user to rapidly scan the results; 2) the user interface for this task should be designed to exploit human visual processing and to allow for rapid feedback; and 3) the system can be made even more efficient by using relevance feedback to learn the user's preferences.

the system is able to: (1) extract the most important information from video and images; (2) automatically create a visual index for efficient search; and (3) allow a user to rapidly scan and select the best results.

developing systems that can efficiently search through very large collections of visual data.
how to make video search more efficient and effective.
how to best combine the complementary strengths of humans and computers in order to achieve the most effective retrieval.

the Informedia video retrieval system is the most advanced and comprehensive system in the world for searching through video.
the system is an excellent tool for the rapid retrieval of video content.
the system is a very effective way to search for video clips, and is a good demonstration of how a user can take advantage of the system's automatic organization of the images.

the human is very effective at searching video, but the system is not.

we have developed a video retrieval system that can be used to search a video archive of about 1 million hours of material, and that can return a ranked list of video segments that are relevant to a query within 10 seconds.
the system has been designed to support a variety of search tasks and user preferences.
The main takeaway from our work is that
video search can be made more efficient by exploiting human visual scanning capabilities.
a combination of automatic image processing, and a human in the loop, can be very efficient for video search.
a human is a better judge of relevance than a computer, and the combination is more effective than the sum of its parts.
